answer: An agent market serving farms in a meadow, boats at a wharf, and sensors on a rocky ledge requires every bidding identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days. Each bond permits only one active bid, so creating extra names grants no free bidding capacity. An attacker running 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds and forgo using that capital elsewhere for a month, making a flood of fake bidders costly even when account creation is free.
